Nina (ruby-sdk): FYI I hit a weird onboarding snag with the Ruby sample app. The quickstart link in README points to the old auth flow and the gem retries behave differently when the token is rotated.
Sam (devex): ah, ugh. Which README link? the GH quickstart or the gem docs?
Nina (ruby-sdk): GH quickstart. It still shows using `REDWOOD_API_KEY` in env and suggests a one-time `bundle exec ruby quickstart.rb` but our hosted tokens are short-lived for trials now. If the SDK gets a 401 it retries once, but doesn't refresh creds so requests keep failing.
Alex (infra): did CI catch this? seemed unrelated to infra but could be an SDK test gap.
Nina (ruby-sdk): CI didn't fail for the sampleapp because tests mock the client. I reproduced locally with real token rotation:

```
# reproduce steps
1) start sampleapp with valid token
2) revoke token from dashboard
3) make a second request -> got 401
```

Observed: SDK does `rescue HTTPUnauthorized` -> retry the same request once -> still 401 -> bubble up. No automatic refresh mechanism.
Sam (devex): ok makes sense. Two separate issues: (1) README has stale onboarding link / flow; (2) SDK retry behavior should either surface a clear error or attempt refresh if a refresh hook is available.
Nina (ruby-sdk): yeah. I can send a small PR to update README to mention short-lived tokens and how to configure a refresh callback. For the SDK change I'm thinking a non-breaking opt-in: `client = Redwood::Client.new(..., token_refresh: -> { fetch_new_token })` so retry would call that lambda before retrying.
Alex (infra): that sounds reasonable and backwards compatible. CI-wise we'll need a small matrix job to exercise the retry path but using a fake refresh hook in tests. CI Bot: Jenkins/ci-matrix #42 started for branch nina/token-refresh-proposal.
Sam (devex): nice. Can you also add a short integration smoke in the sampleapp docs showing the `token_refresh` example? makes onboarding smoother.
Nina (ruby-sdk): yes. I'll open two PRs: one README doc fix in the sampleapp repo, one in the SDK repo adding the optional hook + unit tests. PR titles: "docs(sampleapp): mention short-lived tokens and refresh flow" and "feat(ruby-sdk): optional token_refresh hook for retry on 401"
Sam (devex): ping me when you open them and I'll do review & help land. Also add a changelog note for the SDK so we can call it out in release notes.
Nina (ruby-sdk): will do. I'm also adding a tiny ruby snippet for the README:

```ruby
client = Redwood::Client.new(api_key: ENV["REDWOOD_API_KEY"], token_refresh: -> {
  # call our auth service for a new token
  AuthService.rotate_token_for_user(ENV["USER_ID"])[:token]
})
```

Sam (devex): perfect. That should reduce support tickets.
Alex (infra): I can take the PR for tests later today. If you want, I can also add a CI job template to run the sampleapp smoke against a local mock auth server so we don't rely on dashboard revokes.
Nina (ruby-sdk): that would be great. I'll include a small docker-compose mock auth service in the test fixtures.
CI Bot: Jenkins/ci-matrix #42 passed for nina/token-refresh-proposal (2 min). :white_check_mark:
Sam (devex): awesome, thanks for moving fast @Nina (ruby-sdk) :rocket:
Nina (ruby-sdk): np! will post PR links here in a moment.
Sam (devex): thanks — once merged we should update the quickstart in the portal too to avoid more confusion.
